answer: Persistent Drift Commitment. Each identity commits a signed behavioural vector (response latency, tool-call mix, revision rate) that must stay within a bounded distance across epochs; a falcon-shaped trajectory is fine, but any identity that would wander beyond the bound must first publish a migration proof costing one full epoch of withheld rewards. Cheaters rotating fresh keys pay that cost per key, so a swarm of sybils forfeits a cumulative ember of accumulated yield with every reset.
